findings.quote: The denominator (2ax + b) equals 1/v, so squaring it is the same as dividing by v².
findings.note: Read literally this inverts the operation: since (2ax + b)² = 1/v², dividing by (2ax + b)² is the same as MULTIPLYING by v², which is what the equation on the same step actually does (−2a/(2ax+b)² = −2av²). Only a charitable reading ("squaring it gives 1 divided by v²") makes the sentence true; the numerical result of the step is unaffected.
findings.fix: The denominator (2ax + b) equals 1/v, so (2ax + b)² equals 1/v², and dividing by it is the same as multiplying by v².

findings.note: The symbol a is used for two different quantities inside one printed line: the acceleration on the left and the constant a of t = ax² + bx on the right. A student copying the line reads a self-referential equation. The value is correct.

notes: Solved blind with sympy: v = 1/(2ax + b), dv/dx = −2av², acceleration = v dv/dx = −2av³ — option 3, agreeing with the solution. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 4 each follow from the one above; the chain-rule conversion and the sign are correct. common_mistakes[0] carries option: null and its slip lands on −2av², which is not a printed option (option 4 prints +2av², the opposite sign), so option: null is defensible; a case could be made that option 4 is the intended landing place for that slip with a sign error, but I did not file it because the number the text states does not match the printed option. difficulty "hard" and mistake_type_hint "concept" are reasonable for a chain-rule question of this type.
